decisions.reason: Choosing Danish names for styles does not change which style system must be implemented or its application across all templates.
The candidate already has a message-23 MODIFY setting style_names_language to Danish, so the cross-Requirement effect is fully represented and no additional or edited Event is needed.
The style-name language decision does not change the required copy-paste stability behavior, source templates, migration target, or robustness standard.
Danish style names do not change Tab-driven level transitions, list applicability, hierarchy structure, or nested alignment.
The language used for style names does not alter bullet dimensions, balance, vertical alignment, or scaling behavior.
The style-name language decision does not alter the requirement that pasted content remain within page margins.
Danish style naming does not change numbered or multilevel list alignment behavior.
The style-name language decision does not change manual line-break behavior after pasted content.
The decision to use Danish style names does not resolve or modify table paste stability, column boundaries, or the existing technical ambiguity.
Style-name language does not change the supported Word for Windows environment or the operational-reliability requirement.
